description: Creates a rent.dev account and answers its API key, shown this once (store it; it stays valid until revoked), with the MCP URL and the Authorization header that unlocks its account tools, and a three-line REST quickstart. Go on over REST with the key now: `next_step` creates a sandbox. `reconnect` is your MCP client's `/mcp` block with the key in it (pass `client`; without it, the generic URL and header): a client that can add a server or a header mid-session uses it at once, any other in its next session. To be able to retry, pass idempotency_key, a random value you keep (a UUID will do): if the answer is lost, call again with the same value within 24 hours and you get the same account with a new API key that replaces the first, not a second account. That holds while the account is untouched (its key never used, nothing bound to it, no money in); after that the repeat is refused with idempotency_key_reused and answers no key. Without idempotency_key every call creates a new account. The account starts with a zero balance unless a promotion gives it promotional credit (rent_get_balance shows it): a call that needs more credit than it has answers 402 with a card pay link and an x402 top-up, or use rent_topup with the key. While a limit is set, one network address can create only a limited number of free accounts in 24 hours; past it the call answers 429 signup_limit with retry_after.

client.description: Your MCP client, so that `reconnect` is its own block: claude, claude-ai, chatgpt, codex, cursor, vscode, visualstudio, copilot, gemini, windsurf, cline, zed, opencode, goose, qwen, droid, amp, kiro, warp, continue, antigravity, kilo, crush, lmstudio, devin, http, stdio. `http` is any other client, `stdio` one that only starts local servers.

idempotency_key.description: A random value you choose and keep, such as a UUID, so the signup can be repeated without making a second account. Treat it as a secret for 24 hours: while the account is untouched, whoever sends it gets a new key to the account. The same value works as the Idempotency-Key header of POST /v1/accounts.

name: rent_signup

url.description: The MCP endpoint; send the header there for its account tools.

next_step.description: Run this now: it creates a sandbox with this key and a 3600 second timeout.

quickstart.description: REST calls, in order: balance, create, exec.

reconnect.description: How your client reaches `/mcp` with this key.

client.description: `client`, or `http` when it was left out.

format.description: `shell`: a command to run once. `json`, `toml`, `yaml`: contents to merge into the file. `form`: the fields of a settings form. `launch`: the command the client starts as a local server.

next.description: What to do after, per the client's docs; null when nothing.

session.description: What the client's docs say about a running session; null when they say nothing.

setup.description: The client's section of the MCP page.

text.description: The client's `/mcp` block, with this key in it. A client that takes no key gets its block without one, and `next` says it signs in to the account instead.

where.description: Where `text` goes: a terminal, a file, or a settings form.

replayed.description: True when this repeats an earlier signup with the same idempotency_key: the same account, with a new API key that replaced the one answered before.
